answer.answerText:
You cannot determine this project’s sprinkler requirement from the building’s size, landmark history, or property-record class alone. For the proposed interior alteration, first establish the approved legal occupancy of the affected space, the filing scope and valuation, and the existing-building code basis; then test the alteration-value triggers and any sprinkler rule for the actual occupancy, fire-area size, and location.

For alteration value, fire-protection compliance is required throughout the building when alterations equal or exceed **60% of existing-building value**, reduced to **50%** for a building containing four or more dwelling units. At **30% to under 60%**—or 30% to under 50% in that dwelling-unit category—the altered portions must comply. A separate trigger applies when alterations to an existing R-1 or R-2 space exceed 50% of that space’s value in a building containing four or more dwelling units. (BC §§ 901.9.4, 901.9.4.1–.3.)

Classify the actual approved/proposed use rather than relying on the property-record “O4” label. Offices and nonproduction testing/research are examples of Group B uses (BC § 304.1), but the supplied enacted text does not include a general Group B sprinkler trigger. The supplied rules do identify triggers for Groups I, R, M, F-1, and S-1, and a separate buildingwide rule for Type IV construction using CLT or SCL. (BC §§ 903.2.4, 903.2.6–.9, 903.2.13.)

Temporary sprinkler measures during alteration or demolition are governed by the NYC Fire Code and BC Chapter 33, not by the supplied text alone. (BC § 903.2.12.)
answer.conclusion: You cannot determine this project’s sprinkler requirement from the building’s size, landmark history, or property-record class alone. supportedPoints.heading: Alteration value can require fire-protection upgrades
supportedPoints.explanation: BC 901.9.4 directs alteration work to the value-based provisions. If alterations equal or exceed 60 percent of existing-building value—or 50 percent for a building containing four or more dwelling units—the entire building must comply with Chapter 9 fire-protection requirements as if newly erected. At the stated 30-percent-to-under-60-percent range, or 30-percent-to-under-50-percent range for that dwelling-unit category, the altered portions must comply. A building containing four or more dwelling units also has a separate trigger where alterations to an existing R-1 or R-2 space exceed 50 percent of that space’s value.

supportedPoints.heading: Actual occupancy, area, and location control the supplied occupancy triggers
supportedPoints.explanation: BC 903.2 identifies the listed automatic-sprinkler locations for new buildings and structures. The supplied provisions require sprinklers in Group I occupancies and Group R fire areas, subject to their stated exceptions; they also establish buildingwide triggers for Group M, Group F-1, and Group S-1 based on fire-area size, combined qualifying area, location more than three stories above grade plane, and specified specialized uses. The approved occupancy and relevant fire-area measurements and locations are therefore necessary to apply these provisions.

supportedPoints.heading: Business-use classification must be established from the actual use
supportedPoints.explanation: BC 304.1 includes offices and laboratories for nonproduction testing and research among Business Group B uses. That classification depends on the actual use of the affected space, not the property-record building class.

supportedPoints.heading: Type IV CLT/SCL construction has a separate buildingwide trigger
supportedPoints.explanation: A building utilizing Type IV construction with CLT or SCL must have an NFPA 13 automatic sprinkler system throughout if it is more than three stories above grade plane. A Group B floor exceeding 28,500 square feet is also a trigger. This rule applies only if the building’s actual construction classification and materials meet its stated condition.

supportedPoints.heading: Construction-period sprinkler duties are governed elsewhere
supportedPoints.explanation: For construction, alteration, or demolition operations, BC 903.2.12 directs required automatic sprinkler systems to the NYC Fire Code and BC Chapter 33.

missingFacts: The approved-record basis for the legal occupancy and actual approved/proposed use of the affected space; this determines which occupancy-specific sprinkler rule may apply.
The proposed filing scope, including affected floors, rooms, and fire areas, and whether the work installs, alters, removes, or leaves sprinkler coverage unchanged.
The alteration value, existing-building value, and—if applicable—the value of an existing R-1 or R-2 space, needed to test the 30%, 50%, and 60% thresholds.

citations.title: 901.9.4 Additional requirements based on value of alterations.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 901.9.4 901.9.4 Additional requirements based on value of alterations. Fire protection systems shall be provided to buildings and spaces in accordance with the provisions of Sections 901.9.4.1 through 901.9.4.3.

citations.relevance: Establishes the alteration-value pathways for fire-protection compliance.

citations.title: 901.9.4.1 Alterations requiring fire protection systems throughout a building.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 901.9.4.1 901.9.4.1 Alterations requiring fire protection systems throughout a building. If the value of alterations to the building equals or exceeds 60 percent of the value of the existing building, or, in the case of a building containing 4 or more dwelling units, 50 percent of the value of the existing building, the entire building shall be made to comply with the fire protection requirements of this chapter as if it were hereafter erected.

citations.relevance: Establishes the alteration-value pathways for fire-protection compliance.

citations.title: 901.9.4.2 Alterations requiring fire protection systems in the space being altered.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 901.9.4.2 901.9.4.2 Alterations requiring fire protection systems in the space being altered. If the value of alterations of a space is between 30 percent and 60 percent of the value of the existing building, or, in the case of a building containing 4 or more dwelling units, if the value of alterations of a space is between 30 percent and 50 percent of the value of the existing building, those portions of the building being altered shall be made to comply with the fire protection requirements of this chapter.

citations.relevance: Establishes the alteration-value pathways for fire-protection compliance.

citations.title: 901.9.4.3 Additional requirements for buildings containing 4 or more dwelling units.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 901.9.4.3 901.9.4.3 Additional requirements for buildings containing 4 or more dwelling units. For buildings containing 4 or more dwelling units, if the value of alterations to an existing space classified in Occupancy Group R-1 or R-2 exceeds 50 percent of the value of the space, such space shall be made to comply with the fire protection requirements of this chapter.

citations.relevance: Establishes the alteration-value pathways for fire-protection compliance.

citations.title: 903.2 Where required.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2 903.2 Where required. Approved automatic sprinkler systems in new buildings and structures shall be provided in the locations described in Sections 903.2.1 through 903.2.13. Exceptions: 1. Sprinklers shall not be required in electrical equipment rooms where all of the following conditions are met: 1.1. The room is dedicated to electrical equipment only. 1.2 Only dry-type electrical equipment is used. 1.3 Equipment is installed in a 2-hour fire-rated enclosure including protection for penetrations. 1.4 No combustible storage is permitted to be stored in the room. 2. Sprinklers shall not be permitted in elevator machine rooms and elevator machinery spaces. 3. Sprinklers shall not be required in rooms and spaces protected by an alternative fire suppression system in accordance with the New York City Fire Code and Section 904 of this code.

citations.relevance: Establishes the supplied new-building sprinkler framework and listed occupancy-specific triggers.

citations.title: 903.2.6 Group I.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.6 903.2.6 Group I. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided in Group I occupancies. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings with a main use or dominant occupancy of Group I. Exceptions: 1. An automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 903.3.1.2 or 903.3.1.3 shall be allowed in Group I-1 facilities if located in an I-1 occupancy building or a residential building, provided such building is six stories or less in height. 2. An automatic sprinkler system is not required where Group I-4 day care facilities are at the level of exit discharge and where every room where care is provided has not fewer than one exterior exit door. 3. In buildings where Group I-4 day care is provided on levels other than the level of exit discharge, an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 shall be installed on the entire floor where care is provided, all floors between the level of care and the level of exit discharge, and all floors below the level of exit discharge other than areas classified as an open parking garage.

citations.relevance: Establishes the supplied new-building sprinkler framework and listed occupancy-specific triggers.

citations.title: 903.2.8 Group R.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.8 903.2.8 Group R. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed in Group R fire areas. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings with a main use or dominant occupancy of Group R. Exception: An automatic sprinkler system shall not be required in detached one- and two-family dwellings and multiple single-family dwellings (town houses), provided that such structures are not more than three stories above grade plane in height and have separate means of egress.

citations.relevance: Establishes the supplied new-building sprinkler framework and listed occupancy-specific triggers.

citations.title: 903.2.7 Group M.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.7 903.2.7 Group M. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout buildings containing a Group M occupancy where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. Where a Group M fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ); 2. Where a Group M fire area is located more than three stories above grade plane. 3. Where the combined area of all Group M fire areas on all floors, including any mezzanines, exceeds 24,000 square feet (2229.7 m 2 ). 4. A Group M occupancy used for the display and sale of upholstered furniture or mattresses exceeds 5,000 square feet (464.5 m 2 ).

citations.relevance: Establishes the supplied new-building sprinkler framework and listed occupancy-specific triggers.

citations.title: 903.2.4 Group F.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.4 903.2.4 Group F. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all buildings containing a Group F occupancy where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. Where a Group F-1 fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ); 2. Where a Group F-1 fire area is located more than three stories above grade plane; 3. Where the combined area of all Group F-1 fire areas on all floors, including any mezzanines, exceeds 24,000 square feet (2229.7 m 2 ); 4. Where required by Section 280 of the New York State Labor Law for "factory buildings" defined in Section 2 of such law; or 5. Where a Group F-1 occupancy used for the manufacture of upholstered furniture or mattresses exceeds 2,500 square feet (232.3 m 2 ).

citations.relevance: Establishes the supplied new-building sprinkler framework and listed occupancy-specific triggers.

citations.title: 903.2.9 Group S-1.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.9 903.2.9 Group S-1. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all buildings containing a Group S-1 occupancy where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. A Group S-1 fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ). 2. The building is greater than 1,000 square feet (92.9 m 2 ) in area and the main use or dominant occupancy is Group S-1. 3. A Group S-1 fire area is located more than three stories above grade plane. 4. The combined area of all Group S-1 fire areas on all floors, including any mezzanines, exceeds 24,000 square feet (2229.7 m 2 ). 5. A Group S-1 fire area used for the storage of commercial motor vehicles where the fire area exceeds 5,000 square feet (464.5 m 2 ). 6. A Group S-1 occupancy used for the storage of upholstered furniture or mattresses exceeds 2,500 square feet (232.3 m 2 ).

citations.relevance: Establishes the supplied new-building sprinkler framework and listed occupancy-specific triggers.

citations.title: 304.1 Business Group B.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 304.1 304.1 Business Group B. Business Group B occupancy includes, among others, the use of a building or structure, or a portion thereof, for office, professional, service-type transactions, or for conducting public or civic services, including the incidental storage of records and accounts and the incidental storage of limited quantities of stocks of goods for office use or purposes. Business Group B occupancies shall include, but not be limited to, the following: Airport traffic control towers Ambulatory care facilities Animal hospitals, kennels, pounds, veterinary clinics and pet shops Banks Barber and beauty shops Civic administration offices Clinic-outpatient, including group medical centers, and neighborhood family care centers Custodial care facilities with fewer than 75 persons, providing care to persons over the age of 2, where no more than four occupants are incapable of responding to an emergency situation without physical assistance from staff Dry cleaning and laundries; pick-up and delivery stations and self-service Educational occupancies for students above the 12th grade, where not classified in Group A. Such occupancy may be used occasionally for educational purposes offered to children through the 12th grade Electronic data processing Laboratories; nonproduction testing and research, as per Section 427 Libraries when not classified in Group E Motor vehicle showrooms Offices Post offices Photocopying and printing shops using electronic printing equipment Professional services (architects, attorneys, dentists, physicians, engineers, etc.) Radio and television stations not admitting an audience Telephone exchanges Training and skill development not in a school or academic program (this shall include, but not be limited to, tutoring centers, martial arts studios, gymnastics and similar uses regardless of the ages served, and where not classified as a Group A occupancy) (Am. L.L. 2015/078, 9/2/2015 , eff. 12/31/2015 )

citations.relevance: Identifies offices and nonproduction testing/research as examples of Business Group B uses.

citations.title: 903.2.13 Type IV construction with cross-laminated timber (CLT) or structural composite lumber (SCL).

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.13 903.2.13 Type IV construction with cross-laminated timber (CLT) or structural composite lumber (SCL). Automatic sprinkler systems in accordance with NFPA 13 shall be required throughout buildings utilizing Type IV construction with CLT or SCL as follows: 1. In all occupancies where the building is more than three stories above grade plane. 2. In Group B occupancies, where a floor exceeds 28,500 square feet (2647.7 m 2 ).

citations.relevance: Establishes the Type IV CLT/SCL sprinkler triggers.

citations.title: 903.2.12 During construction.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.12 903.2.12 During construction. Automatic sprinkler systems required during construction, alteration and demolition operations shall be provided in accordance with the New York City Fire Code and Chapter 33 of this code .

citations.relevance: Directs construction-period sprinkler requirements to the NYC Fire Code and BC Chapter 33.

sources.text: 901.9.4 901.9.4 Additional requirements based on value of alterations. Fire protection systems shall be provided to buildings and spaces in accordance with the provisions of Sections 901.9.4.1 through 901.9.4.3.

903.2.13 903.2.13 Type IV construction with cross-laminated timber (CLT) or structural composite lumber (SCL). Automatic sprinkler systems in accordance with NFPA 13 shall be required throughout buildings utilizing Type IV construction with CLT or SCL as follows: 1. In all occupancies where the building is more than three stories above grade plane. 2. In Group B occupancies, where a floor exceeds 28,500 square feet (2647.7 m 2 ).

903.2.6 903.2.6 Group I. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided in Group I occupancies. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings with a main use or dominant occupancy of Group I. Exceptions: 1. An automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 903.3.1.2 or 903.3.1.3 shall be allowed in Group I-1 facilities if located in an I-1 occupancy building or a residential building, provided such building is six stories or less in height. 2. An automatic sprinkler system is not required where Group I-4 day care facilities are at the level of exit discharge and where every room where care is provided has not fewer than one exterior exit door. 3. In buildings where Group I-4 day care is provided on levels other than the level of exit discharge, an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 shall be installed on the entire floor where care is provided, all floors between the level of care and the level of exit discharge, and all floors below the level of exit discharge other than areas classified as an open parking garage.

903.2.8 903.2.8 Group R. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed in Group R fire areas. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings with a main use or dominant occupancy of Group R. Exception: An automatic sprinkler system shall not be required in detached one- and two-family dwellings and multiple single-family dwellings (town houses), provided that such structures are not more than three stories above grade plane in height and have separate means of egress.

903.2.7 903.2.7 Group M. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout buildings containing a Group M occupancy where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. Where a Group M fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ); 2. Where a Group M fire area is located more than three stories above grade plane. 3. Where the combined area of all Group M fire areas on all floors, including any mezzanines, exceeds 24,000 square feet (2229.7 m 2 ). 4. A Group M occupancy used for the display and sale of upholstered furniture or mattresses exceeds 5,000 square feet (464.5 m 2 ).

903.2.4 903.2.4 Group F. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all buildings containing a Group F occupancy where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. Where a Group F-1 fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ); 2. Where a Group F-1 fire area is located more than three stories above grade plane; 3. Where the combined area of all Group F-1 fire areas on all floors, including any mezzanines, exceeds 24,000 square feet (2229.7 m 2 ); 4. Where required by Section 280 of the New York State Labor Law for "factory buildings" defined in Section 2 of such law; or 5. Where a Group F-1 occupancy used for the manufacture of upholstered furniture or mattresses exceeds 2,500 square feet (232.3 m 2 ).

903.2 903.2 Where required. Approved automatic sprinkler systems in new buildings and structures shall be provided in the locations described in Sections 903.2.1 through 903.2.13. Exceptions: 1. Sprinklers shall not be required in electrical equipment rooms where all of the following conditions are met: 1.1. The room is dedicated to electrical equipment only. 1.2 Only dry-type electrical equipment is used. 1.3 Equipment is installed in a 2-hour fire-rated enclosure including protection for penetrations. 1.4 No combustible storage is permitted to be stored in the room. 2. Sprinklers shall not be permitted in elevator machine rooms and elevator machinery spaces. 3. Sprinklers shall not be required in rooms and spaces protected by an alternative fire suppression system in accordance with the New York City Fire Code and Section 904 of this code.

903.2.9 903.2.9 Group S-1. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all buildings containing a Group S-1 occupancy where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. A Group S-1 fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ). 2. The building is greater than 1,000 square feet (92.9 m 2 ) in area and the main use or dominant occupancy is Group S-1. 3. A Group S-1 fire area is located more than three stories above grade plane. 4. The combined area of all Group S-1 fire areas on all floors, including any mezzanines, exceeds 24,000 square feet (2229.7 m 2 ). 5. A Group S-1 fire area used for the storage of commercial motor vehicles where the fire area exceeds 5,000 square feet (464.5 m 2 ). 6. A Group S-1 occupancy used for the storage of upholstered furniture or mattresses exceeds 2,500 square feet (232.3 m 2 ).

304.1 304.1 Business Group B. Business Group B occupancy includes, among others, the use of a building or structure, or a portion thereof, for office, professional, service-type transactions, or for conducting public or civic services, including the incidental storage of records and accounts and the incidental storage of limited quantities of stocks of goods for office use or purposes. Business Group B occupancies shall include, but not be limited to, the following: Airport traffic control towers Ambulatory care facilities Animal hospitals, kennels, pounds, veterinary clinics and pet shops Banks Barber and beauty shops Civic administration offices Clinic-outpatient, including group medical centers, and neighborhood family care centers Custodial care facilities with fewer than 75 persons, providing care to persons over the age of 2, where no more than four occupants are incapable of responding to an emergency situation without physical assistance from staff Dry cleaning and laundries; pick-up and delivery stations and self-service Educational occupancies for students above the 12th grade, where not classified in Group A. Such occupancy may be used occasionally for educational purposes offered to children through the 12th grade Electronic data processing Laboratories; nonproduction testing and research, as per Section 427 Libraries when not classified in Group E Motor vehicle showrooms Offices Post offices Photocopying and printing shops using electronic printing equipment Professional services (architects, attorneys, dentists, physicians, engineers, etc.) Radio and television stations not admitting an audience Telephone exchanges Training and skill development not in a school or academic program (this shall include, but not be limited to, tutoring centers, martial arts studios, gymnastics and similar uses regardless of the ages served, and where not classified as a Group A occupancy) (Am. L.L. 2015/078, 9/2/2015 , eff. 12/31/2015 )

903.2.12 903.2.12 During construction. Automatic sprinkler systems required during construction, alteration and demolition operations shall be provided in accordance with the New York City Fire Code and Chapter 33 of this code .

AMBULATORY CARE FACILITY. Buildings or portions thereof used to provide medical, surgical, psychiatric, nursing or similar care on a less than 24-hour basis to individuals who are rendered incapable of self-preservation by the services provided. AUTOMATIC SPRINKLER SYSTEM. A fire suppression or control device that operates automatically when its heat-activated element is heated to its thermal rating or above, allowing water to discharge over a specified area. COMMERCIAL MOTOR VEHICLE. A motor vehicle used to transport passengers or goods where the motor vehicle: 1. Has a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 pounds (4540 kg) or more; or 2. Is designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver. CUSTODIAL CARE FACILITY. A building or part thereof occupied by persons, on less than a 24-hour basis and not overnight, who because of age, disability or other reasons, receive personal care services by individuals other than parents or guardians, relatives by blood, marriage, domestic partnership, or adoption, in a place other than the home of the person cared for. FIRE PROTECTION SYSTEM. Approved devices, equipment and systems or combinations of systems used to detect a fire, activate an alarm, extinguish or control a fire, control or manage smoke and products of a fire or any combination thereof. LABORATORY, NONPRODUCTION. See Section 427.4. OPEN PARKING GARAGE . A structure or portion of a structure with the openings as described in Section 406 . 5 . 2 that is used for the parking or storage of private motor vehicles as described in Section 406 . 5.3 . STORY ABOVE GRADE PLANE . Any story having its finished floor surface entirely above grade plane , except that a basement shall also be considered a story above grade plane ( see " Story " and " Basement ").

901.9.4.1 901.9.4.1 Alterations requiring fire protection systems throughout a building. If the value of alterations to the building equals or exceeds 60 percent of the value of the existing building, or, in the case of a building containing 4 or more dwelling units, 50 percent of the value of the existing building, the entire building shall be made to comply with the fire protection requirements of this chapter as if it were hereafter erected.

901.9.4.3 901.9.4.3 Additional requirements for buildings containing 4 or more dwelling units. For buildings containing 4 or more dwelling units, if the value of alterations to an existing space classified in Occupancy Group R-1 or R-2 exceeds 50 percent of the value of the space, such space shall be made to comply with the fire protection requirements of this chapter.

901.9.4.2 901.9.4.2 Alterations requiring fire protection systems in the space being altered. If the value of alterations of a space is between 30 percent and 60 percent of the value of the existing building, or, in the case of a building containing 4 or more dwelling units, if the value of alterations of a space is between 30 percent and 50 percent of the value of the existing building, those portions of the building being altered shall be made to comply with the fire protection requirements of this chapter.

903.3.1.2 903.3.1.2 NFPA 13R sprinkler systems. Where allowed in buildings of Group R, up to and including six stories in height, automatic sprinkler systems shall be installed throughout in accordance with NFPA 13R. The number of stories of Group R occupancies constructed in accordance with Sections 510.2 and 510.4 shall be measured from the horizontal assembly creating separate buildings.

903.3.1.3 903.3.1.3 NFPA 13D sprinkler systems. Where allowed, automatic sprinkler systems in one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses, up to and including six stories in height, shall be installed throughout in accordance with NFPA 13D.

903.3.1.1 903.3.1.1 NFPA 13 sprinkler systems. Where the provisions of this code require that a building or portion thereof be equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with this section, sprinklers shall be installed throughout in accordance with NFPA 13 except as provided in Sections 903.3.1.1.1 and 903.2 of this code. (Am. L.L. 2023/077, 6/11/2023, eff. 6/11/2023) Editor's note: For related unconsolidated provisions, see Appendix A at L.L. 2023/077 .

sources.text: 903.2 903.2 Where required. Approved automatic sprinkler systems in new buildings and structures shall be provided in the locations described in Sections 903.2.1 through 903.2.13. Exceptions: 1. Sprinklers shall not be required in electrical equipment rooms where all of the following conditions are met: 1.1. The room is dedicated to electrical equipment only. 1.2 Only dry-type electrical equipment is used. 1.3 Equipment is installed in a 2-hour fire-rated enclosure including protection for penetrations. 1.4 No combustible storage is permitted to be stored in the room. 2. Sprinklers shall not be permitted in elevator machine rooms and elevator machinery spaces. 3. Sprinklers shall not be required in rooms and spaces protected by an alternative fire suppression system in accordance with the New York City Fire Code and Section 904 of this code.

903.2.3 903.2.3 Group E. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided for Group E occupancies as follows: 1. Throughout all Group E fire areas greater than 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ) in area. 2. Throughout every portion of educational buildings below the level of exit discharge. Exception: An automatic sprinkler system is not required in any fire area or area below the level of exit discharge where every classroom throughout the building has not fewer than one exterior exit door at ground level without intervening corridors, passageways, interior exit stairways or ramps or exit passageways.

903.2.12 903.2.12 During construction. Automatic sprinkler systems required during construction, alteration and demolition operations shall be provided in accordance with the New York City Fire Code and Chapter 33 of this code .
903.2.5 903.2.5 Group H. Automatic sprinkler systems shall be provided in high-hazard occupancies as required in the New York City Fire Code and Sections 903.2.5.1 through 903.2.5.3 of this code .

903.2.8 903.2.8 Group R. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed in Group R fire areas. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings with a main use or dominant occupancy of Group R. Exception: An automatic sprinkler system shall not be required in detached one- and two-family dwellings and multiple single-family dwellings (town houses), provided that such structures are not more than three stories above grade plane in height and have separate means of egress.

903.2.13 903.2.13 Type IV construction with cross-laminated timber (CLT) or structural composite lumber (SCL). Automatic sprinkler systems in accordance with NFPA 13 shall be required throughout buildings utilizing Type IV construction with CLT or SCL as follows: 1. In all occupancies where the building is more than three stories above grade plane. 2. In Group B occupancies, where a floor exceeds 28,500 square feet (2647.7 m 2 ).

903.2.6 903.2.6 Group I. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided in Group I occupancies. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings with a main use or dominant occupancy of Group I. Exceptions: 1. An automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 903.3.1.2 or 903.3.1.3 shall be allowed in Group I-1 facilities if located in an I-1 occupancy building or a residential building, provided such building is six stories or less in height. 2. An automatic sprinkler system is not required where Group I-4 day care facilities are at the level of exit discharge and where every room where care is provided has not fewer than one exterior exit door. 3. In buildings where Group I-4 day care is provided on levels other than the level of exit discharge, an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 shall be installed on the entire floor where care is provided, all floors between the level of care and the level of exit discharge, and all floors below the level of exit discharge other than areas classified as an open parking garage.

903.2.4 903.2.4 Group F. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all buildings containing a Group F occupancy where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. Where a Group F-1 fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ); 2. Where a Group F-1 fire area is located more than three stories above grade plane; 3. Where the combined area of all Group F-1 fire areas on all floors, including any mezzanines, exceeds 24,000 square feet (2229.7 m 2 ); 4. Where required by Section 280 of the New York State Labor Law for "factory buildings" defined in Section 2 of such law; or 5. Where a Group F-1 occupancy used for the manufacture of upholstered furniture or mattresses exceeds 2,500 square feet (232.3 m 2 ).

903.2.11 903.2.11 Specific building areas and hazards. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed for building design or hazards in the locations set forth in Sections 903.2.11.1 through 903.2.11.13.

903.2.10 903.2.10 Group S-2. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings greater than 5,000 square feet (464.5 m 2 ) in areas where the main use or dominant occupancy is Group S-2.

AUTOMATIC SPRINKLER SYSTEM. A fire suppression or control device that operates automatically when its heat-activated element is heated to its thermal rating or above, allowing water to discharge over a specified area. EXIT DISCHARGE. That portion of a means of egress system between the termination of an exit and a public way. INTERIOR EXIT STAIRWAY. An exit component that serves to meet one or more means of egress design requirements, such as required number of exits or exit access travel distance, and provides for a protected path of egress travel to the exit discharge or public way. OPEN EXTERIOR SPACE . See Section 1002 . 1 . 2 . OPEN PARKING GARAGE . A structure or portion of a structure with the openings as described in Section 406 . 5 . 2 that is used for the parking or storage of private motor vehicles as described in Section 406 . 5.3 . STORY ABOVE GRADE PLANE . Any story having its finished floor surface entirely above grade plane , except that a basement shall also be considered a story above grade plane ( see " Story " and " Basement "). STRUCTURAL COMPOSITE LUMBER. Structural member manufactured using wood elements bonded together with exterior adhesives. Examples of structural composite lumber are: Laminated strand lumber (LSL). A composite of wood strand elements with wood fibers primarily oriented along the length of the member, where the least dimension of the wood strand elements is 0.10 inch (2.54 mm) or less and their average lengths not less than 150 times the least dimension of the wood strand elements. Laminated veneer lumber (LVL). A composite of wood veneer sheet elements with wood fibers primarily oriented along the length of the member, where the veneer element thicknesses are 0.25 inches (6.4 mm) or less. Oriented strand lumber (OSL). A composite of wood strand elements with wood fibers primarily oriented along the length of the member, where the least dimension of the wood strand elements is 0.10 inch (2.54 mm) or less and their average lengths not less than 75 times and less than 150 times the least dimension of the strand elements. Parallel strand lumber (PSL). A composite of wood strand elements with wood fibers primarily oriented along the length of the member where the least dimension of the wood strand elements is 0.25 inches (6.4 mm) or less and their average lengths not less than 300 times the least dimension of the wood strand elements. TRANSIT. The moving or transporting of a crane from one jobsite to another.

903.2.1 903.2.1 Group A. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout buildings and portions thereof used as Group A occupancies as provided in this section. For Group A-1, A-2, A-3 and A-4 occupancies, the automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout the floor area where the Group A-1, A-2, A-3 or A-4 occupancy is located, and in all floors between the Group A occupancy and the level of exit discharge. For Group A-5 occupancies, the automatic sprinkler system shall be provided in the spaces indicated in Section 903.2.1.5. In all Group A occupancies providing live entertainment, dressing rooms and property rooms used in conjunction with such assembly occupancy shall be provided with an automatic sprinkler system. Stages shall comply with Section 410.7.
903.2.2 903.2.2 Group B. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed for Group B occupancies as provided in Sections 903.2.2.1 and 903.2.2.2. (Am. L.L. 2015/078, 9/2/2015, eff. 12/31/2015)

903.2.7 903.2.7 Group M. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout buildings containing a Group M occupancy where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. Where a Group M fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ); 2. Where a Group M fire area is located more than three stories above grade plane. 3. Where the combined area of all Group M fire areas on all floors, including any mezzanines, exceeds 24,000 square feet (2229.7 m 2 ). 4. A Group M occupancy used for the display and sale of upholstered furniture or mattresses exceeds 5,000 square feet (464.5 m 2 ).

903.2.9 903.2.9 Group S-1. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all buildings containing a Group S-1 occupancy where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. A Group S-1 fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ). 2. The building is greater than 1,000 square feet (92.9 m 2 ) in area and the main use or dominant occupancy is Group S-1. 3. A Group S-1 fire area is located more than three stories above grade plane. 4. The combined area of all Group S-1 fire areas on all floors, including any mezzanines, exceeds 24,000 square feet (2229.7 m 2 ). 5. A Group S-1 fire area used for the storage of commercial motor vehicles where the fire area exceeds 5,000 square feet (464.5 m 2 ). 6. A Group S-1 occupancy used for the storage of upholstered furniture or mattresses exceeds 2,500 square feet (232.3 m 2 ).

903.2.5.1 903.2.5.1 General. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed in Group H occupancies. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings with a main use or dominant occupancy of Group H.

903.2.5.3 903.2.5.3 Pyroxylin plastics. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided in buildings, or portions thereof, where cellulose nitrate film or pyroxylin plastics are manufactured, stored or handled in quantities exceeding 100 pounds (45.4 kg).

answer.answerText:
**No.** Keeping the approved Group B office use and having no enlargement eliminates the supplied change-of-use and enlargement paths, and an office does not fall within the supplied Group B ambulatory-health-care or animal-service provisions (BC §§ 901.9.2–.3, 903.2.2–.2.2). But that does not settle sprinklers.

If this is a **prior-code building**, BC 901.9 applies its Chapter 9 provisions to alterations. The alteration-value rules can then require Chapter 9 compliance: at **60% or more** of existing-building value, the whole building must comply as newly erected; at **30% to under 60%**, the altered portions must comply (BC §§ 901.9, 901.9.4.1–.2). The supplied text also contains separate sprinkler triggers based on exterior Fire Department access, a story with occupant load of 30 or more at least 55 feet above Fire Department vehicle access, and qualifying Type IV CLT/SCL construction (BC §§ 903.2.11.2,.11.7,.13). The facts needed to test those triggers are not supplied.
answer.conclusion: **No.** Keeping the approved Group B office use and having no enlargement eliminates the supplied change-of-use and enlargement paths, and an office does not fall within the supplied Group B ambulatory-health-care or animal-service provisions (BC §§ 901.9.2–.3, 903.2.2–.2.2). But that does not settle sprinklers.

supportedPoints.heading: Retained Group B office use and no enlargement do not invoke the stated paths
supportedPoints.explanation: For prior-code buildings, BC 901.9.2 requires Chapter 9 fire-protection systems for a change in main use, dominant occupancy, occupancy-group classification, or space usage. The stated hypothetical retains Group B office use. BC 901.9.3 addresses enlarged portions, and the hypothetical states there is no enlargement. The supplied Group B rule directs sprinkler requirements to ambulatory health care facilities and animal service facilities; the stipulated office use is neither.

supportedPoints.heading: Prior-code-building alteration value can trigger Chapter 9 compliance
supportedPoints.explanation: BC 901.9 makes Chapter 9 applicable to alterations and changes of use or occupancy in prior-code buildings. If that scope applies, alterations valued at 60 percent or more of existing-building value require the entire building to comply with Chapter 9 as if newly erected; alterations valued from 30 percent to under 60 percent require the altered portions to comply.

supportedPoints.heading: Other supplied sprinkler triggers depend on unresolved building conditions
supportedPoints.explanation: The supplied provisions require sprinklers for specified above-grade stories below 100 feet without the stated direct exterior access; throughout a building with a story having occupant load of 30 or more at least 55 feet above the lowest Fire Department vehicle access; and throughout qualifying Type IV CLT/SCL buildings. For Type IV CLT/SCL buildings, the rule applies where the building is more than three stories above grade plane or, in Group B, where a floor exceeds 28,500 square feet.

answer.explanation: If this is a **prior-code building**, BC 901.9 applies its Chapter 9 provisions to alterations. The alteration-value rules can then require Chapter 9 compliance: at **60% or more** of existing-building value, the whole building must comply as newly erected; at **30% to under 60%**, the altered portions must comply (BC §§ 901.9, 901.9.4.1–.2). The supplied text also contains separate sprinkler triggers based on exterior Fire Department access, a story with occupant load of 30 or more at least 55 feet above Fire Department vehicle access, and qualifying Type IV CLT/SCL construction (BC §§ 903.2.11.2,.11.7,.13). The facts needed to test those triggers are not supplied.
missingFacts: Whether the building is a prior-code building, which determines whether BC 901.9 and its alteration-value provisions apply.
Alteration value as a percentage of the existing building’s value, if BC 901.9 applies.
For BC 903.2.11.2: whether applicable above-grade stories are below 100 feet in height and lack the specified direct exterior access at the required spacing.
For BC 903.2.11.7: whether any story has an occupant load of 30 or more and its finished-floor height above the lowest Fire Department vehicle access.
For BC 903.2.13: whether the building utilizes Type IV construction with CLT or SCL and, if applicable, the area of each Group B floor.

citations.title: 901.9 Special provisions for prior code buildings.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 901.9 901.9 Special provisions for prior code buildings. The provisions of this chapter shall apply to alterations and changes of use or occupancy to prior code buildings in accordance with Sections 901.9.1 through 901.9.6.

citations.relevance: BC 901.9 limits its alteration and change-of-use scope to prior-code buildings.

citations.title: 901.9.2 Additional requirements based on change of occupancy or use.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 901.9.2 901.9.2 Additional requirements based on change of occupancy or use. Fire protection systems governed by this chapter shall be provided: 1. To the entire building as if the building were hereafter erected, where a change is made in the main use or dominant occupancy of such building. 2. Throughout a space, where a change is made in the occupancy group classification or usage of the space.

citations.relevance: No-change-of-use and no-enlargement application.

citations.title: 901.9.3 Additional requirements for enlargements.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 901.9.3 901.9.3 Additional requirements for enlargements. Fire protection systems shall be provided in enlarged portions of a building and where this chapter would require such systems in new construction for a space or building. Exception. Section 901.9.3 shall not require sprinklers to be installed in enlarged portions of unsprinklered buildings to be occupied exclusively as one- or two-family dwellings. This exception shall not apply where sprinklers are otherwise required by the provisions of Sections 901.9.2 or 901.9.4.

citations.relevance: No-change-of-use and no-enlargement application.

citations.title: 903.2.2 Group B.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.2 903.2.2 Group B. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed for Group B occupancies as provided in Sections 903.2.2.1 and 903.2.2.2. (Am. L.L. 2015/078, 9/2/2015, eff. 12/31/2015)

citations.relevance: Supplied Group B sprinkler categories.

citations.title: 903.2.2.1 Ambulatory health care facilities.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.2.1 903.2.2.1 Ambulatory health care facilities. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout all fire areas containing a Group B ambulatory health care facility occupancy. In buildings where ambulatory care is provided on levels other than the level of exit discharge, an automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout the entire floor where such care is provided as well as all floors below, and all floors between the level of ambulatory care and the nearest level of exit discharge, including the level of exit discharge. (L.L. 2015/078, 9/2/2015, eff. 12/31/2015)

citations.relevance: Supplied Group B sprinkler categories.

citations.title: 903.2.2.2 Animal service facilities.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.2.2 903.2.2.2 Animal service facilities. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided for animal service facilities. Exceptions: 1. Animal service facilities that provide 24 hour in-person supervision of animals sheltered therein and are equipped with smoke alarms. 2. Animal service facilities that were in operation on or before December 31, 2016, and are equipped with an automatic smoke detection system. (L.L. 2015/078, 9/2/2015, eff. 12/31/2015)

citations.relevance: Supplied Group B sprinkler categories.

citations.title: 901.9.4 Additional requirements based on value of alterations.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 901.9.4 901.9.4 Additional requirements based on value of alterations. Fire protection systems shall be provided to buildings and spaces in accordance with the provisions of Sections 901.9.4.1 through 901.9.4.3.

citations.relevance: Alteration-value thresholds.

citations.title: 901.9.4.1 Alterations requiring fire protection systems throughout a building.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 901.9.4.1 901.9.4.1 Alterations requiring fire protection systems throughout a building. If the value of alterations to the building equals or exceeds 60 percent of the value of the existing building, or, in the case of a building containing 4 or more dwelling units, 50 percent of the value of the existing building, the entire building shall be made to comply with the fire protection requirements of this chapter as if it were hereafter erected.

citations.relevance: Alteration-value thresholds.

citations.title: 901.9.4.2 Alterations requiring fire protection systems in the space being altered.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 901.9.4.2 901.9.4.2 Alterations requiring fire protection systems in the space being altered. If the value of alterations of a space is between 30 percent and 60 percent of the value of the existing building, or, in the case of a building containing 4 or more dwelling units, if the value of alterations of a space is between 30 percent and 50 percent of the value of the existing building, those portions of the building being altered shall be made to comply with the fire protection requirements of this chapter.

citations.relevance: Alteration-value thresholds.

citations.title: 903.2.11.2 Other above-grade stories.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.11.2 903.2.11.2 Other above-grade stories. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout every above-grade story of buildings below a height of 100 feet (30 480 mm), other than the first story or ground floor, on which access is not provided directly from the outdoors by at least one window or readily identifiable access panel within each 50 feet (15 240 mm) or fraction thereof of horizontal length of every wall that fronts on a street or frontage space required pursuant to Section 501.3.1.

citations.relevance: Separate supplied sprinkler triggers based on access, height and occupant load, and Type IV CLT/SCL construction.

citations.title: 903.2.11.7 Buildings 55 feet (16 764 mm) or more in height.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.11.7 903.2.11.7 Buildings 55 feet (16 764 mm) or more in height. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings that have one or more stories with an occupant load of 30 or more located 55 feet (16 764 mm) or more above the lowest level of Fire Department vehicle access, measured to the finished floor. Exceptions: 1. Open parking structures without any other occupancy groups, unless otherwise required. 2. Occupancies in Group F-2, unless required by the New York State Department of Labor.

citations.relevance: Separate supplied sprinkler triggers based on access, height and occupant load, and Type IV CLT/SCL construction.

citations.title: 903.2.13 Type IV construction with cross-laminated timber (CLT) or structural composite lumber (SCL).

supportingPassages.selectedText: 903.2.13 903.2.13 Type IV construction with cross-laminated timber (CLT) or structural composite lumber (SCL). Automatic sprinkler systems in accordance with NFPA 13 shall be required throughout buildings utilizing Type IV construction with CLT or SCL as follows: 1. In all occupancies where the building is more than three stories above grade plane. 2. In Group B occupancies, where a floor exceeds 28,500 square feet (2647.7 m 2 ).

citations.relevance: Separate supplied sprinkler triggers based on access, height and occupant load, and Type IV CLT/SCL construction.

sources.text: 901.9 901.9 Special provisions for prior code buildings. The provisions of this chapter shall apply to alterations and changes of use or occupancy to prior code buildings in accordance with Sections 901.9.1 through 901.9.6.

903.2 903.2 Where required. Approved automatic sprinkler systems in new buildings and structures shall be provided in the locations described in Sections 903.2.1 through 903.2.13. Exceptions: 1. Sprinklers shall not be required in electrical equipment rooms where all of the following conditions are met: 1.1. The room is dedicated to electrical equipment only. 1.2 Only dry-type electrical equipment is used. 1.3 Equipment is installed in a 2-hour fire-rated enclosure including protection for penetrations. 1.4 No combustible storage is permitted to be stored in the room. 2. Sprinklers shall not be permitted in elevator machine rooms and elevator machinery spaces. 3. Sprinklers shall not be required in rooms and spaces protected by an alternative fire suppression system in accordance with the New York City Fire Code and Section 904 of this code.

903.2.8 903.2.8 Group R. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed in Group R fire areas. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings with a main use or dominant occupancy of Group R. Exception: An automatic sprinkler system shall not be required in detached one- and two-family dwellings and multiple single-family dwellings (town houses), provided that such structures are not more than three stories above grade plane in height and have separate means of egress.

903.2.13 903.2.13 Type IV construction with cross-laminated timber (CLT) or structural composite lumber (SCL). Automatic sprinkler systems in accordance with NFPA 13 shall be required throughout buildings utilizing Type IV construction with CLT or SCL as follows: 1. In all occupancies where the building is more than three stories above grade plane. 2. In Group B occupancies, where a floor exceeds 28,500 square feet (2647.7 m 2 ).

903.2.11.3 903.2.11.3 Other below-grade stories. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout every first basement or cellar story below grade of buildings on which access is not provided directly from the outdoors within each 100 feet (30 480 mm) or fraction thereof of horizontal length of every wall that fronts on a street or frontage space required pursuant to Section 501.3.1. Exceptions: 1. One- and two-family dwellings need not provide direct access. 2. Any building classified in Occupancy Group R-2 not more than three stories in height and with not more than two dwelling units on any story need not provide direct access when such first basement or cellar story is used for dwelling units or for uses accessory to the residential use in the building. 3. Except as provided in Exception 2, above, for Group R-1 and R-2 occupancies, only one direct access from the outdoors to the first basement or cellar story consisting of a stair or door shall be required when such story is used for dwelling units or for uses accessory to the residential use in the building.

903.2.11.7 903.2.11.7 Buildings 55 feet (16 764 mm) or more in height. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings that have one or more stories with an occupant load of 30 or more located 55 feet (16 764 mm) or more above the lowest level of Fire Department vehicle access, measured to the finished floor. Exceptions: 1. Open parking structures without any other occupancy groups, unless otherwise required. 2. Occupancies in Group F-2, unless required by the New York State Department of Labor.

901.9.5.4 901.9.5.4 Additional requirements for enlargements of buildings with no existing standpipe systems. Where the alteration involves the addition of stories to a building with no existing standpipe system, standpipes shall be provided to all stair shafts in accordance with this chapter. Exception. Standpipes are not required where: 1. the alteration involves the addition of only one story; 2. the completed building does not exceed 7 stories; and 3. the completed building does not exceed 85 feet (25.9 m) in height.

903.2.5.2 903.2.5.2 Group H-5 occupancies. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings containing Group H-5 occupancies. The design of the sprinkler system shall not be less than that required by this code for the occupancy hazard classifications in accordance with Table 903.2.5.2 . Where the design area of the sprinkler system consists of a corridor protected by one row of sprinklers, the maximum number of sprinklers required to be calculated is 13. Table 903.2.5.2 Group H-5 Sprinkler Design Criteria Location Occupancy Hazard Classification Fabrication areas Ordinary Hazard Group 2 Service corridors Ordinary Hazard Group 2 Storage rooms without dispensing Ordinary Hazard Group 2 Storage rooms with dispensing Extra Hazard Group 2 Corridors Ordinary Hazard Group 2

903.2.11.2 903.2.11.2 Other above-grade stories. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout every above-grade story of buildings below a height of 100 feet (30 480 mm), other than the first story or ground floor, on which access is not provided directly from the outdoors by at least one window or readily identifiable access panel within each 50 feet (15 240 mm) or fraction thereof of horizontal length of every wall that fronts on a street or frontage space required pursuant to Section 501.3.1.

903.2.4.3 903.2.4.3 Group F-1 fire areas. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout any Group F-1 occupancy fire area where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. The fire area exceeds 7,500 square feet (696.8 m 2 ). 2. The fire area of any size is located more than 3 stories above grade.

AUTOMATIC SPRINKLER SYSTEM. A fire suppression or control device that operates automatically when its heat-activated element is heated to its thermal rating or above, allowing water to discharge over a specified area. DWELLING UNIT. A single unit consisting of one or more habitable rooms and occupied or arranged to be occupied as a unit separate from all other units within a dwelling. FABRICATION AREA . An area within a semiconductor fabrication facility in which processes using hazardous production materials are conducted . OCCUPANT LOAD . The number of persons for which the means of egress of a building or portion thereof is designed . SERVICE CORRIDOR . A fully enclosed passage other than one designated as a required means of egress , through which HPM can be moved during handling . STORAGE ROOM . See Section 427 . 4 . STORY ABOVE GRADE PLANE . Any story having its finished floor surface entirely above grade plane , except that a basement shall also be considered a story above grade plane ( see " Story " and " Basement "). STRUCTURAL COMPOSITE LUMBER. Structural member manufactured using wood elements bonded together with exterior adhesives. Examples of structural composite lumber are: Laminated strand lumber (LSL). A composite of wood strand elements with wood fibers primarily oriented along the length of the member, where the least dimension of the wood strand elements is 0.10 inch (2.54 mm) or less and their average lengths not less than 150 times the least dimension of the wood strand elements. Laminated veneer lumber (LVL). A composite of wood veneer sheet elements with wood fibers primarily oriented along the length of the member, where the veneer element thicknesses are 0.25 inches (6.4 mm) or less. Oriented strand lumber (OSL). A composite of wood strand elements with wood fibers primarily oriented along the length of the member, where the least dimension of the wood strand elements is 0.10 inch (2.54 mm) or less and their average lengths not less than 75 times and less than 150 times the least dimension of the strand elements. Parallel strand lumber (PSL). A composite of wood strand elements with wood fibers primarily oriented along the length of the member where the least dimension of the wood strand elements is 0.25 inches (6.4 mm) or less and their average lengths not less than 300 times the least dimension of the wood strand elements.

901.9.1 901.9.1 Additions, alterations or repairs. Additions, alterations, renovations or repairs to existing systems shall conform to that required for new systems without requiring the existing system to comply with all of the requirements of this code, except as otherwise required in Sections 901.9.2 through 901.9.6. Additions, alterations or repairs shall not cause an existing installation to become unsafe, hazardous or overloaded.

901.9.2 901.9.2 Additional requirements based on change of occupancy or use. Fire protection systems governed by this chapter shall be provided: 1. To the entire building as if the building were hereafter erected, where a change is made in the main use or dominant occupancy of such building. 2. Throughout a space, where a change is made in the occupancy group classification or usage of the space.

901.9.3 901.9.3 Additional requirements for enlargements. Fire protection systems shall be provided in enlarged portions of a building and where this chapter would require such systems in new construction for a space or building. Exception. Section 901.9.3 shall not require sprinklers to be installed in enlarged portions of unsprinklered buildings to be occupied exclusively as one- or two-family dwellings. This exception shall not apply where sprinklers are otherwise required by the provisions of Sections 901.9.2 or 901.9.4.

901.9.4 901.9.4 Additional requirements based on value of alterations. Fire protection systems shall be provided to buildings and spaces in accordance with the provisions of Sections 901.9.4.1 through 901.9.4.3.

901.9.4.1 901.9.4.1 Alterations requiring fire protection systems throughout a building. If the value of alterations to the building equals or exceeds 60 percent of the value of the existing building, or, in the case of a building containing 4 or more dwelling units, 50 percent of the value of the existing building, the entire building shall be made to comply with the fire protection requirements of this chapter as if it were hereafter erected.

901.9.4.2 901.9.4.2 Alterations requiring fire protection systems in the space being altered. If the value of alterations of a space is between 30 percent and 60 percent of the value of the existing building, or, in the case of a building containing 4 or more dwelling units, if the value of alterations of a space is between 30 percent and 50 percent of the value of the existing building, those portions of the building being altered shall be made to comply with the fire protection requirements of this chapter.

901.9.4.3 901.9.4.3 Additional requirements for buildings containing 4 or more dwelling units. For buildings containing 4 or more dwelling units, if the value of alterations to an existing space classified in Occupancy Group R-1 or R-2 exceeds 50 percent of the value of the space, such space shall be made to comply with the fire protection requirements of this chapter.

901.9.5 901.9.5 Additional provisions. In buildings or spaces not otherwise required to provide fire protection systems in accordance with this chapter, fire protection systems shall be provided for the types of alterations described in Sections 901.9.5.1 through 901.9.5.4.

901.9.6 901.9.6 Seismic supports. The determination as to whether seismic requirements apply to an alteration shall be made in accordance with the 1968 Building Code and interpretations by the department relating to such determinations. Any applicable seismic loads and requirements shall be permitted to be determined in accordance with Chapter 16 of this code or the 1968 Building Code and Reference Standard RS 9-6 of such code. Section BC 902: Definitions
903.2.2 903.2.2 Group B. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed for Group B occupancies as provided in Sections 903.2.2.1 and 903.2.2.2. (Am. L.L. 2015/078, 9/2/2015, eff. 12/31/2015)

903.2.2.1 903.2.2.1 Ambulatory health care facilities. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout all fire areas containing a Group B ambulatory health care facility occupancy. In buildings where ambulatory care is provided on levels other than the level of exit discharge, an automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout the entire floor where such care is provided as well as all floors below, and all floors between the level of ambulatory care and the nearest level of exit discharge, including the level of exit discharge. (L.L. 2015/078, 9/2/2015, eff. 12/31/2015)

903.2.2.2 903.2.2.2 Animal service facilities. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided for animal service facilities. Exceptions: 1. Animal service facilities that provide 24 hour in-person supervision of animals sheltered therein and are equipped with smoke alarms. 2. Animal service facilities that were in operation on or before December 31, 2016, and are equipped with an automatic smoke detection system. (L.L. 2015/078, 9/2/2015, eff. 12/31/2015)

903.2.1 903.2.1 Group A. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout buildings and portions thereof used as Group A occupancies as provided in this section. For Group A-1, A-2, A-3 and A-4 occupancies, the automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout the floor area where the Group A-1, A-2, A-3 or A-4 occupancy is located, and in all floors between the Group A occupancy and the level of exit discharge. For Group A-5 occupancies, the automatic sprinkler system shall be provided in the spaces indicated in Section 903.2.1.5. In all Group A occupancies providing live entertainment, dressing rooms and property rooms used in conjunction with such assembly occupancy shall be provided with an automatic sprinkler system. Stages shall comply with Section 410.7.

903.2.3 903.2.3 Group E. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided for Group E occupancies as follows: 1. Throughout all Group E fire areas greater than 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ) in area. 2. Throughout every portion of educational buildings below the level of exit discharge. Exception: An automatic sprinkler system is not required in any fire area or area below the level of exit discharge where every classroom throughout the building has not fewer than one exterior exit door at ground level without intervening corridors, passageways, interior exit stairways or ramps or exit passageways.

903.2.4 903.2.4 Group F. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all buildings containing a Group F occupancy where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. Where a Group F-1 fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ); 2. Where a Group F-1 fire area is located more than three stories above grade plane; 3. Where the combined area of all Group F-1 fire areas on all floors, including any mezzanines, exceeds 24,000 square feet (2229.7 m 2 ); 4. Where required by Section 280 of the New York State Labor Law for "factory buildings" defined in Section 2 of such law; or 5. Where a Group F-1 occupancy used for the manufacture of upholstered furniture or mattresses exceeds 2,500 square feet (232.3 m 2 ).
903.2.5 903.2.5 Group H. Automatic sprinkler systems shall be provided in high-hazard occupancies as required in the New York City Fire Code and Sections 903.2.5.1 through 903.2.5.3 of this code .

903.2.6 903.2.6 Group I. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided in Group I occupancies. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings with a main use or dominant occupancy of Group I. Exceptions: 1. An automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 903.3.1.2 or 903.3.1.3 shall be allowed in Group I-1 facilities if located in an I-1 occupancy building or a residential building, provided such building is six stories or less in height. 2. An automatic sprinkler system is not required where Group I-4 day care facilities are at the level of exit discharge and where every room where care is provided has not fewer than one exterior exit door. 3. In buildings where Group I-4 day care is provided on levels other than the level of exit discharge, an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 shall be installed on the entire floor where care is provided, all floors between the level of care and the level of exit discharge, and all floors below the level of exit discharge other than areas classified as an open parking garage.

903.2.7 903.2.7 Group M. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout buildings containing a Group M occupancy where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. Where a Group M fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ); 2. Where a Group M fire area is located more than three stories above grade plane. 3. Where the combined area of all Group M fire areas on all floors, including any mezzanines, exceeds 24,000 square feet (2229.7 m 2 ). 4. A Group M occupancy used for the display and sale of upholstered furniture or mattresses exceeds 5,000 square feet (464.5 m 2 ).

sources.text: 903.2 903.2 Where required. Approved automatic sprinkler systems in new buildings and structures shall be provided in the locations described in Sections 903.2.1 through 903.2.13. Exceptions: 1. Sprinklers shall not be required in electrical equipment rooms where all of the following conditions are met: 1.1. The room is dedicated to electrical equipment only. 1.2 Only dry-type electrical equipment is used. 1.3 Equipment is installed in a 2-hour fire-rated enclosure including protection for penetrations. 1.4 No combustible storage is permitted to be stored in the room. 2. Sprinklers shall not be permitted in elevator machine rooms and elevator machinery spaces. 3. Sprinklers shall not be required in rooms and spaces protected by an alternative fire suppression system in accordance with the New York City Fire Code and Section 904 of this code.

901.9 901.9 Special provisions for prior code buildings. The provisions of this chapter shall apply to alterations and changes of use or occupancy to prior code buildings in accordance with Sections 901.9.1 through 901.9.6.

903.2.3 903.2.3 Group E. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided for Group E occupancies as follows: 1. Throughout all Group E fire areas greater than 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ) in area. 2. Throughout every portion of educational buildings below the level of exit discharge. Exception: An automatic sprinkler system is not required in any fire area or area below the level of exit discharge where every classroom throughout the building has not fewer than one exterior exit door at ground level without intervening corridors, passageways, interior exit stairways or ramps or exit passageways.

903.2.11.7 903.2.11.7 Buildings 55 feet (16 764 mm) or more in height. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings that have one or more stories with an occupant load of 30 or more located 55 feet (16 764 mm) or more above the lowest level of Fire Department vehicle access, measured to the finished floor. Exceptions: 1. Open parking structures without any other occupancy groups, unless otherwise required. 2. Occupancies in Group F-2, unless required by the New York State Department of Labor.

903.2.11.3 903.2.11.3 Other below-grade stories. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout every first basement or cellar story below grade of buildings on which access is not provided directly from the outdoors within each 100 feet (30 480 mm) or fraction thereof of horizontal length of every wall that fronts on a street or frontage space required pursuant to Section 501.3.1. Exceptions: 1. One- and two-family dwellings need not provide direct access. 2. Any building classified in Occupancy Group R-2 not more than three stories in height and with not more than two dwelling units on any story need not provide direct access when such first basement or cellar story is used for dwelling units or for uses accessory to the residential use in the building. 3. Except as provided in Exception 2, above, for Group R-1 and R-2 occupancies, only one direct access from the outdoors to the first basement or cellar story consisting of a stair or door shall be required when such story is used for dwelling units or for uses accessory to the residential use in the building.

903.2.1.3 903.2.1.3 Group A-3. An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided for Group A-3 occupancies where any one of the following conditions exists: 1. The fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1114.8 m 2 ). 2. The fire area has an occupant load of 300 or more. 3. The aggregate occupant load of all fire areas occupied by Group A, located on any given floor other than the level of exit discharge, is 300 or more. Exception: Areas used exclusively as participant sports areas where the main floor area is located at the same level as the level of exit discharge of the main entrance and exit.

903.2.5.2 903.2.5.2 Group H-5 occupancies. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout buildings containing Group H-5 occupancies. The design of the sprinkler system shall not be less than that required by this code for the occupancy hazard classifications in accordance with Table 903.2.5.2 . Where the design area of the sprinkler system consists of a corridor protected by one row of sprinklers, the maximum number of sprinklers required to be calculated is 13.
